page_title: Realtime Django Part 2: Build a Chat application with django, RabbitMQ and Vue.js (Authentication and User Management)

summary.title: Realtime Django Part 2: Build a Chat application with django, RabbitMQ and Vue.js (Authentication and User Management)
summary.one_liner: You learn how to add user registration and token authentication to a Django backend with djoser, and connect a Vue.js frontend to it while resolving CORS errors with django-cors-headers.
takeaways: Install djoser and configure it with DRF TokenAuthentication to get REST endpoints for user creation and token login.
Scaffold a Vue app with vue-cli (webpack template with vue-router) and use a global beforeEach guard to redirect unauthenticated users to a login/signup component.
Call the Django auth endpoints from Vue using jQuery ajax, storing the returned token in sessionStorage.
Understand the same origin policy and fix cross-origin errors by enabling django-cors-headers (CORS_ORIGIN_ALLOW_ALL for development, whitelist for production).
Switch from sessionStorage to localStorage to persist the token across browser restarts, and remove it with removeItem for logout.
summary.summary: The article is part 2 of a series building a realtime chat app with Django, RabbitMQ and Vue.js. It sets up user management and authentication by installing djoser, enabling DRF token authentication and running migrations. On the frontend it scaffolds a Vue app with vue-cli and vue-router, adds a navigation guard that checks for a token, and builds a Bootstrap 4 login/signup component that calls the API via jQuery ajax. It then explains the CORS error encountered during signup and fixes it with django-cors-headers, closing with notes on logout and the next part on models and the chat API.
